newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Daiei suffers sharp slide in profits.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Daiei suffers sharp slide in profits.

text.p: Japan's largest supermarket chain operator reported a sharp fall in profits on Tuesday due to poor sales of food and clothes, and announced a set of measures to get its finances into better shape.

Kobe-based Daiei Inc said that its parent current profit for the six months to August 31 dropped 49 percent year on year to 61.3 billion yen ($547 million), while sales dropped 1.2 percent to 1.24 trillion yen ($11.0 billion) from the year-earlier period.
Current profits are pre-tax and include losses or gains on non-operating activities such as investments in stocks.

The company's sales have been hit by a food poisoning epidemic that swept Japan earlier this year, triggering health fears about certain fresh foodstuffs, and by an unusually cool summer, which depressed sales of clothing and outdoor goods.
Daiei also announced plans to improve its finances.
Chairman Isao Nakauchi said the retailer would seek to list the shares of several of its subsidiaries as soon as possible to diversify its means of fund raising.

He also said Daiei would consider reducing the number of banks through which it does the bulk of its financial transactions. The company said it was considering ending its business relationship with Sakura Bank Ltd, reducing the number of banks it deals with to just Tokai, Sanwa, Sumitomo and Fuji.
"We hope to finalise our plan on conducting business with banks before the end of this year," Nakauchi told a news conference where Daiei announced its earnings results.
Nakauchi said the company is borrowing 200 billion yen ($1.78 billion) from Sakura and hopes to pay back all of those loans within two to three years.

Daiei's interest-bearing debts totalled 600.8 billion yen ($5.36 billion) as of the end of August, down from 629.3 billion yen ($5.61 billion) at the end of February. The company expects the level of debt to be about the same at the end of the 1996/97 business year as it was at the end of August.
To improve its earnings situation, the company earlier this year sold part of its shareholdings in banks and department stores, raising some 20 billion yen ($178 million).

In late August, Daiei sold about 80 percent of the shares it held in major Japanese department store Takashimaya Co Ltd, worth 14 billion yen ($125 million), to Japanese department store Printemps Ginza SA, which is wholly owned by Daiei.
Daiei also some sold shares in the five banks with which it has close business relationships.
